evals.prompt: I need to click the 'Delete' button inside a specific row of a data table. The row is identified by the project name 'Apollo'. The table renders a loading skeleton first, then the real rows. My current locator page.locator('.row .btn-delete') keeps failing with a strict mode violation. Give me the locator.
evals.expected_output: An anchor-and-drill locator: scope to the row by its accessible content, then drill to the button by role. Uses getByRole over CSS, avoids XPath, and explains the skeleton/duplicate-element cause of the strict-mode violation.
expectations: The proposed locator uses getByRole for the button rather than a CSS class selector
The locator is scoped (anchored) to the row container first and then drilled into, rather than addressing the button from the page root
The row is identified by accessible content (name/text/row role) rather than by a CSS class
No XPath is used anywhere in the answer
It explains that the strict-mode violation comes from more than one matching element, e.g. skeleton and real content briefly coexisting
It does not propose .first(), .nth(), or an index as the primary fix
It does not propose page.waitForTimeout or any hard wait
It does not propose page.evaluate or direct DOM manipulation

evals.prompt: Write the locators for a page object for a settings form that has: a Save button, an email input labelled 'Email address', a Country dropdown (Radix UI), a validation error message, and a success toast.
evals.expected_output: Locator getters following the priority hierarchy (role > text > label > placeholder > alt > title > test-id as last resort), with the Radix dropdown handled by its documented recipe, and feedback selectors (error + success) present.
expectations: The email input uses getByLabel (or getByRole with an accessible name), not a CSS selector or placeholder
data-testid is used only where semantic locators genuinely cannot work, not as the default
The Radix dropdown is handled with an explicit strategy for portalled or re-rendering content rather than a naive direct locator
Both a validation-error locator and a success-message locator are present
The locators are exposed as getters and carry no JSDoc comments on them
